feed.title: Awesome Security & AI Research: a weekly vetted briefing
feed.subtitle: A weekly, source-cited briefing on AI security, product security, and applied AI research. Every finding is vetted, distilled to one lesson and one action, and filed by field. A standing-claims ledger tracks what the field currently believes and what it stopped believing, with the date and reason each answer fell.

entry.title: OpenJDK Base64 decoder flaw Java4Shell corrupts memory on AVX-512 CPUs
entry.summary: Patch JDK 17, 21, 25 and 27 (including bundled runtimes and container images), prioritizing x86-64 hosts whose CPUs report avx512vbmi.

entry.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension on Cursor Marketplace plants persistent SSH backdoor
entry.summary: An AI coding-assistant extension from the official vendor, served by an editor marketplace, ran with full user rights when loaded, so hunt for integrated development environment (IDE) extension hosts writing to ~/.ssh and LaunchAgents and do not treat uninstalling as remediation.

entry.title: N-able takes hosted N-central offline after researcher publishes 33 zero-day exploits
entry.summary: Remote management platforms hold admin access to many customer networks, so a public exploit release for one can force an outage and an emergency shutdown.

entry.title: SafeDep tracks wfx stealer pushed into 8,093+ repos, likely via stolen tokens
entry.summary: If any repo you own got a wfx-docs PR or a reverted 'ci: refresh build cache' commit, revoke the author's tokens, rotate all reachable secrets and hunt for AWS/Entra backdoors.

entry.title: N-able investigates new N-central exploits that work against hotfixed on-premise servers
entry.summary: MSP (managed service provider) teams running on-premise N-central should turn off the Legacy API now, as probing for the new root remote code execution exploit has already been observed.

entry.title: Chainguard details wfx stealer that backdoors cloud roles and can forge checks
entry.summary: With a stolen write token, pinning and pull request review do nothing, so limit what a CI runner holds and audit cloud trust after any wfx hit.

entry.title: Researcher releases SignDrop Windows zero-day exploit granting SYSTEM privileges
entry.summary: Defenders relying on antimalware self-protection should know this public exploit can reportedly be used to turn off any antivirus or endpoint detection and response (EDR) product, with no patch yet.

entry.title: Check Point ships hotfixes for a zero-day exploited for root access
entry.summary: Gateway owners should patch now and hunt for compromise, because attackers chained this flaw with another to reach root and then wipe a VMware ESXi host.

entry.title: Red Hat Quay flaws (CVSS 9.8, 9.9) let attackers overwrite private images
entry.summary: Quay registries reachable by untrusted clients, even internal ones, can be used to poison every system that pulls their images, so apply the fix and hunt for planted keys.

entry.title: Google Project Zero shortens its disclosure deadline to 30 days by 2028
entry.summary: A major research team now treats AI-accelerated exploitation as the default, so vendors need to fix every reported bug within 30 to 60 days and close the patch gap, whatever the bug's severity.

entry.title: PostgreSQL fixes a 22-year-old type confusion bug that enables code execution
entry.summary: Any role that can create objects should be treated as a possible route to code on the database host until the server and its extensions are both upgraded.

entry.title: Harness choice alone can double an agent's cost
entry.summary: On the same model and task, the harness alone changed cost up to about 2x at similar accuracy, and coding agents' first call ranges from about 1.9k to 32k input tokens.

entry.title: Learn per-repo cost controls from past coding agent runs
entry.summary: A controller that learns from earlier runs in the same repository which tools to prune, which short notes to inject and when to stop unproductive failure loops cut coding-agent cost by 18-31% on SWE-Bench with comparable task success.

entry.title: Use one-hour cache markers when sessions pause over five minutes
entry.summary: Harnesses that write 5-minute prompt-cache markers re-buy their whole context after an idle gap longer than five minutes, while harnesses with 1-hour markers kept about 86% cache hits after a 390-second pause.

entry.title: Constrained decoding wins for structured output, not TOON
entry.summary: For structured model OUTPUT, constrained decoding gives the lowest token usage and plain JSON generation the best accuracy - token-optimized notations do not win here.
